tutorial.welcomeBody: Make yourself at home: build your furniture pieces one by one, arrange them in a 3D room and, when you like the result, send them straight into a request. Take the short mission tour — two minutes and you'll know everything the studio can do.

createPiece.title: Your first piece
createPiece.body: Press “New piece” in the left panel, pick a body type and shape it with the sliders. When you save, the piece lands right in the room.

orbit.title: Take a walk around it
orbit.body: Hold the mouse down on an empty part of the room and move it to turn the view around; scroll to zoom in and out.

movePiece.title: Put it in its place
movePiece.body: Grab the piece and drag it across the floor. For precision: arrow keys move it 1 cm (Shift = 5), and in the floating panel you can type the exact distance to each wall.

rotatePiece.title: Face it the right way
rotatePiece.body: Select the piece with a click, then press R — or the rotate button in the floating panel.

addOpening.title: Cut a door or a window
addOpening.body: In the bar under the room, click a door, window or outlet to put it on a wall — or drag it straight onto the wall you want.

adjustOpening.title: Fit it to the wall
adjustOpening.body: With the opening selected, slide it along the wall or adjust its dimensions in the panel. R moves it to the next wall.

styleRoom.title: Make the room yours
styleRoom.body: Same bottom bar: set the room's width and depth to the centimetre and pick the wall and floor colours.

addScene.title: One more room
addScene.body: A project can hold several rooms. Press “New room” above the scene — then hop between them from the tabs, each with its own pieces.

undo.title: No regrets
undo.body: Broke something? Ctrl+Z steps back, Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes. Try one step back right now.
undo.hint: Nothing to undo yet — make a small change first (nudge the piece with an arrow key), then press Ctrl+Z.

tutorial.finaleBody: You've covered everything that matters. A few things worth knowing before you go:
tutorial.finaleTip1: “My drafts” saves the project to your account — pick it up again anytime.
tutorial.finaleTip2: F = fullscreen, and the floating panel moves by its grip, wherever you like it.
tutorial.finaleTip3: “Add to request” sends the whole room into the form — companies see exactly what you built.
tutorial.finaleReplay: Replay the tour anytime from the “?” button above the room.

SketchGuidePage.subtitle: No architect needed — four simple steps give the companies everything they need to quote accurately. The sheet on the left shows exactly what your sketch needs to include.

measure.title: Measure the walls
measure.body: Take the length of every wall and the ceiling height. Measure at floor level, corner to corner.

draw.tip: It doesn't have to be to scale — the numbers matter, not pretty drawing.

mark.tip: An ✕ for sockets, a double line for windows — like the socket mark on the sheet.

info.title: Melamine chipboard
info.body: Melamine-faced chipboard — the standard for cabinet carcasses, with the best price-to-durability ratio.
info.pros1: The best price per linear metre — your budget goes to fittings instead
info.pros2: Hundreds of decors: plain colours, wood grains, even concrete looks
info.pros3: The melamine surface shrugs off everyday scratches
info.cons1: Edges need ABS banding, or they show and wear
info.cons2: Swells if water reaches an unsealed cut

MDF.description: Painted or foil-wrapped fronts, refined look

info.title: Painted/foiled MDF
info.body: Medium-density fibreboard — the right base for painted, routed or foil-wrapped fronts.
info.pros1: Smooth surface — paint goes on evenly, with no board texture
info.pros2: Can be routed: profiles, frames, classic patterns
info.pros3: Edges finish cleanly, no applied banding needed
info.cons1: Costs more than chipboard for the same piece
info.cons2: The boards are heavy — large units need matching hardware

MDF_INFOLIAT.description: PVC foil on routed fronts, easy to keep clean

info.title: Foil-wrapped MDF
info.body: MDF fronts wrapped in heat-pressed PVC foil — routed patterns and a clean look at a moderate price.
info.pros1: The foil keeps water out — works in kitchens and bathrooms
info.pros2: Wipes clean with a cloth, no special products needed
info.pros3: Allows routed fronts, with frames or classic patterns
info.cons1: Next to an oven or hob, the foil can peel over time
info.cons2: A narrower colour palette than painted MDF

info.title: Painted MDF
info.body: Electrostatically painted MDF fronts — any RAL colour, in matte, satin or gloss.
info.pros1: Any colour and sheen — matches the rest of your home exactly
info.pros2: Fine edges with no visible banding — the most refined look
info.pros3: A scratch can be repainted locally, no front replacement
info.cons1: Among the most expensive front options
info.cons2: Paint can chip on a direct knock

MDF_FURNIR.label: Veneered MDF
MDF_FURNIR.description: Natural wood veneer on a stable core

info.title: Veneered MDF
info.body: MDF wrapped in natural wood veneer — the authentic grain of wood, without solid timber's warping risk.
info.pros1: Real wood grain, there to see and to touch
info.pros2: The MDF core won't warp the way solid wood does
info.pros3: Can be stained to the shade you want, just like wood
info.cons1: Rare veneers cost close to solid wood
info.cons2: Deep scratches cut through the thin veneer layer

info.title: Solid wood
info.body: Solid natural timber — the most durable option, with a grain unique to every piece.
info.pros1: Lasts for decades and can always be repaired
info.pros2: Every piece has its own grain — no two are alike
info.pros3: Can be sanded and refinished to look new again
info.cons1: The most expensive material option
info.cons2: Moves with humidity — it can crack or warp

pieceSystems.title: Which opening system?
pieceSystems.subtitle: For this piece's doors and drawers — you can pick several.

info.title: Push-to-open
info.body: Fronts open with a light press, no handles — the line stays completely clean.
info.pros1: Smooth fronts with no handle to break the line
info.pros2: Opens with an elbow when your hands are full
info.cons1: Fingerprints show quickly on smooth fronts
info.cons2: The mechanism needs adjusting more often than a classic hinge

info.title: Sliding systems
info.body: Doors or drawers that glide on rails — no swing space needed, well suited to wardrobes.
info.pros1: The door never swings out — works even right beside the bed
info.pros2: Carries wide, heavy fronts, all the way to the ceiling
info.cons1: Good rails cost more — cheap ones you feel on every open
info.cons2: Needs precise fitting — a skewed rail is heard and felt

info.title: Press latch
info.body: A simple click mechanism — the most affordable handleless opening.
info.pros1: The smallest investment for handleless fronts
info.pros2: A simple mechanism — easy to fit and to replace

MANER.label: Handle

info.title: Classic handles

info.pros2: Thousands of models — handles alone can change the look

info.cons2: Can catch clothes as you pass in narrow spaces

GOLA.label: Gola

info.title: Gola profile
info.body: An aluminium channel set between the fronts — you open from the profile and the front line stays unbroken.
info.pros1: An unbroken line with no handles — the modern kitchen look
info.pros2: Nothing sticks out — nothing to catch as you pass by
info.cons1: Routing and the profile add to the price
info.cons2: Demanding to fit — a job for an experienced team

AVENTOS.label: Aventos (lift-up)

info.title: Aventos system
info.body: Wall-cabinet fronts lift on damped arms — full access, with no open door at head height.
info.pros1: No more open doors to bump into above the worktop
info.pros2: The front stays open at any position until you pull it down
info.cons1: The most expensive opening system
info.cons2: The arms need periodic adjustment to stay balanced

layout.title: What shape is the kitchen?
layout.subtitle: Pick the layout that fits your space.

info.title: Straight kitchen
info.body: All cabinets along one wall — compact, a natural fit for small spaces.
info.pros1: Lowest cost per metre of any layout
info.pros2: Fits narrow kitchens and open-plan living areas
info.pros3: Quick to install: one wall, no corners to solve
info.cons1: The worktop stays short — serious cooking takes organising
info.cons2: Less storage; tall units become almost essential

info.title: L-shaped kitchen
info.body: Cabinets on two walls — a good balance of worktop and circulation.
info.pros1: Sink, hob and fridge sit close — short paths while cooking
info.pros2: Fits most apartments without blocking the walkway
info.pros3: Leaves room for a table or a breakfast corner
info.cons1: The corner is hard to reach without dedicated fittings
info.cons2: Corner systems (carousel, pull-out) add to the price

info.title: U-shaped kitchen
info.body: Cabinets on three sides — maximum storage and worktop.
info.pros1: Storage on three sides — you'll rarely need another cupboard
info.pros2: Generous worktop: cook and prep in parallel
info.pros3: Separate zones for cooking, washing and prep
info.cons1: Feels cramped in rooms under 2.4 m wide
info.cons2: Two corners to solve — each needs fittings or wastes space

info.title: Galley kitchen
info.body: Two facing runs — efficient in pass-through kitchens.
info.pros1: Everything one step away — the layout cooks prefer
info.pros2: Two people can cook without getting in each other's way
info.cons1: The aisle between runs needs at least 1.2 m clear
info.cons2: No room left for a table in the kitchen

hasIsland.title: Do you want an island?

info.title: Kitchen island

info.pros1: Extra worktop and storage, right at the centre of the action
info.pros2: Doubles as a breakfast bar or a spot for guests
info.cons1: Only works in large kitchens — otherwise it blocks circulation
info.cons2: A separate unit and worktop — the cost adds up visibly

info.title: Laminated chipboard worktop
info.body: Chipboard core with a laminated surface — the affordable standard, hundreds of designs.
info.pros1: Lowest price — easy to replace years later without regrets
info.pros2: Hundreds of designs: wood, stone, plain colours
info.cons1: Edges swell if water gets past the sealing
info.cons2: Scratches and dulls visibly in heavy-use areas

info.title: HPL worktop
info.body: High-pressure laminate — far denser and tougher than standard chipboard.
info.pros1: Handles water, scratches and daily wear far better than chipboard
info.pros2: Can be slim, for a clean, modern line
info.cons1: Roughly double the price of a standard laminate top
info.cons2: Narrower range of designs than regular laminate

info.title: Laminate countertop
info.body: Laminated chipboard — the budget option with the widest choice of designs.
info.pros1: The lowest-priced worktop of all
info.pros2: Designs for any style, from wood to concrete
info.cons1: Deep scratches cannot be repaired
info.cons2: Hot pans straight on the top leave marks — use a trivet

info.title: Quartz countertop
info.body: Engineered stone — among the most durable and hygienic worktops.
info.pros1: Nearly impossible to scratch in everyday use
info.pros2: Non-porous surface: doesn't stain, easy to keep hygienic
info.cons1: Among the priciest worktop options
info.cons2: Very heavy — cabinets must be built to carry it

info.title: Granite countertop
info.body: Natural stone — durable, with a unique pattern in every slab.
info.pros1: Natural stone that takes decades of daily use
info.pros2: Every slab has a one-of-a-kind pattern
info.cons1: Needs periodic sealing, or it can stain
info.cons2: High price, and so are transport and fitting

info.title: Wood countertop
info.body: Solid wood — a warm look, cared for with periodic oiling.
info.pros1: Warms up any kitchen — works in modern styles too
info.pros2: Scratches sand out; the top can be refinished any time
info.cons1: Needs regular oiling, especially around the sink
info.cons2: Standing water stains and swells the wood

info.title: Linear closet
info.body: Modules along a single wall — the compact option for a bedroom or hallway.

info.pros2: The lowest-cost configuration
info.cons1: Limited capacity — choose carefully what lives here

info.title: L-shaped closet
info.body: Modules on two walls — puts the corner to work.
info.pros1: Serious capacity without taking over the room
info.pros2: An otherwise wasted corner becomes storage
info.cons1: The corner stays awkward without dedicated modules

info.title: U-shaped closet
info.body: Modules on three sides — maximum storage capacity.
info.pros1: The most storage per square metre
info.pros2: Separate zones: hanging, drawers, shelves
info.cons1: Needs a generous room, or you'll be bumping into doors

info.title: Walk-in closet
info.body: A dedicated room, with modules on several walls.
info.pros1: Your whole wardrobe visible, in one place
info.pros2: Get dressed on the spot, no doors to open
info.cons1: You give up a room, or part of one

info.title: Sliding doors
info.body: Doors that glide on rails — they need no swing space at all.
info.pros1: Sit flush against a bed or wall — zero swing space
info.pros2: One large, continuous surface — great for mirrors too
info.cons1: Good rails cost more — cheap ones wear out fast

info.title: Hinged doors
info.body: Classic hinged doors — full access to the interior.
info.pros1: Open a door and see the whole interior at a glance
info.pros2: Hinges cost less than any sliding system
info.cons1: Open doors need clear space in front of the wardrobe

info.title: Open closet
info.body: Doorless modules — everything visible and within reach.
info.pros1: Grab what you need in a single motion
info.pros2: No doors, no hardware — the lowest cost
info.cons1: Dust settles on clothes — takes constant tidiness

info.body: The classic hanger zone. One metre of rod holds about 10–12 hangers; long dresses need 150–160 cm of free height.

info.title: Drawers
info.body: The priciest interior module: slides, fronts, assembly. Soft-close is worth it in daily-use zones.

info.title: Shelves
info.body: The most affordable modules. Adjustable shelves cost a little extra and pay off quickly.

info.title: Shoe rack
info.body: Tilted shelves with a stopper or pull-out racks. Allow about 20 cm of width per pair.

info.title: Interior accessories

info.pros2: The most affordable option, with easy-to-adjust hinges

info.body: The unit goes all the way up, with no dead space above. Height is measured in several spots — ceilings are rarely perfectly level.

info.pros2: Top shelves take suitcases and seasonal items

info.title: Under-bed drawers

info.title: Upholstered bed
info.body: Frame and headboard wrapped in fabric or eco-leather — soft to the touch, with plenty of colours to pick from. You choose the exact fabric together with the company.

info.title: One or a pair

info.body: Closed cabinets below for what you rarely use, open shelves above for everyday access — the practical balance.
info.pros1: Everything in sight or under cover, by how you use it

info.cons1: Slightly pricier than plain shelves

info.title: Why enclosure matters
info.body: PAL and MDF suffer from moisture, frost and direct sun. On a balcony enclosed with double glazing they behave like indoors; on an open one we recommend exterior-treated solid wood — or rethinking the project.

info.title: Enclosed balcony
info.body: The environment is close to indoors, with one note: sun shines straight through the glass and fades fronts over time.
info.pros1: Any material works, same as the rest of the home
info.pros2: Year-round storage, whatever the weather
info.cons1: Direct sun through the glass fades fronts over time

info.title: Open balcony
info.body: Rain, frost, big temperature swings — tough conditions for any furniture. We recommend exterior-treated solid wood and stainless steel hardware.
info.pros1: Exterior-treated solid wood holds up outside
info.pros2: You keep the open-air feel
info.cons1: PAL and MDF do not survive here, foil-wrapped or not

doorType.title: What doors for the wardrobe?
doorType.subtitle: The choice changes the price and the clearance you need in front of it.

info.title: Sliding doors
info.body: Doors glide on tracks, one past the other — handy when the bed sits close. Track quality decides how smoothly they run for years.
info.pros1: The bed can sit right next to it — zero swing clearance
info.pros2: Large fronts, calm modern look
info.cons1: You see one half at a time, and the bottom track collects dust

info.title: Hinged doors
info.body: The classic solution, on hinges: simple, reliable, cheap to repair. Check you have about 50 cm free in front of the wardrobe.
info.pros1: Open the whole wardrobe at once — see and reach every shelf
info.pros2: The cheapest option, and hinges adjust in minutes
info.cons1: Each door needs ~50 cm of free space to swing open

toCeiling.title: Up to the ceiling, built-in style?
toCeiling.subtitle: The wardrobe closes against the ceiling and reads as built-in furniture.

info.title: Floor-to-ceiling wardrobe
info.body: A built-in look, no dust collecting on top, and seasonal storage up high. The company measures the height in several spots — ceilings are rarely level.
info.pros1: No more dust collecting on top of the wardrobe
info.pros2: The top row takes suitcases and seasonal bedding
info.cons1: You reach the top row only with a step stool

style.subtitle: From a simple unit under the TV to a full-wall composition.

LOW_UNIT.description: One horizontal unit under the TV

info.title: Low TV unit
info.body: A horizontal unit with doors and drawers: console, media collection and cables stay hidden, the TV above.
info.pros1: The smallest budget of the two options
info.pros2: Not fixed to the wall — it moves when you do
info.cons1: Storage is limited to what fits under the TV

MEDIA_WALL.label: Media wall
MEDIA_WALL.description: Panels and units across the wall

info.title: Full media wall
info.body: Decorative panels, wall-hung units, a TV niche and usually LED lighting. Cables run behind the panels.
info.pros1: The wall becomes the centrepiece of the living room
info.pros2: Every cable disappears behind the panels
info.cons1: Cost and installation to match; once mounted, it stays put

info.title: TV on the wall or on the unit
info.body: If the TV goes on the wall, the company prepares the cable route and, if needed, a niche. If it sits on the unit, the top depth matters. You can also decide later, together with the company.

style.title: What bookcase style?
style.subtitle: Open, with base cabinets, or behind glass.

info.title: Open bookcase
info.body: Open shelves — you take the book straight off the shelf. Dust settles on the spines, so plan on regular wiping.
info.pros1: Every book is one reach away, no doors in between
info.pros2: The simplest build — the lowest price
info.cons1: Dust lands straight on the books — regular wiping needed

info.title: With base cabinets
info.body: Solid doors below for files and less sightly things; open shelves above for books and objects.
info.pros1: Clutter lives below, behind doors — only what deserves display stays up
info.pros2: The composition feels balanced: solid below, airy above
info.cons1: Pricier than plain shelving, because of the doors and hardware

info.title: Display bookcase
info.body: Glass doors over the full height — books and objects stay visible, yet sheltered from dust.
info.pros1: Dust never reaches the books — you only wipe the glass
info.pros2: Cherished pieces sit on display, collection-style
info.cons1: The priciest option, and glass shows every fingerprint

info.title: Floor-to-ceiling bookcase
info.body: A whole wall of books — impressive and space-efficient. The top row takes a step stool.

material.subtitle: Wide shelves need a rigid material, or they sag under books.

shape.title: What desk shape?
shape.subtitle: Straight along one wall, or L-shaped in the corner.

info.title: Straight desk
info.body: A worktop along a single wall. For comfortable work: at least 120 cm wide and 60 cm deep.
info.pros1: Fits small rooms and narrow walls
info.pros2: Less material — lower price
info.cons1: With two monitors and paperwork, the top fills up fast

info.title: Corner desk
info.body: The top continues around the corner — one zone for monitors, one kept clear for writing. The corner stops going to waste.
info.pros1: Nearly double the work surface in the same room
info.pros2: Puts the corner — usually dead space — to work
info.cons1: Made for that corner — hard to move to another room

info.title: Organizing the cables
info.body: A tray under the top and discreet cutouts keep cables gathered, so the desk stays clean. Tell the company how many devices you have — monitors, laptop, chargers.

info.title: Shelf riser
info.body: Shelves mounted above the desk for books and files — you use the wall, not the worktop.

bedSize.subtitle: The frame is built around the mattress — we start from its size.

info.title: Standard sizes
info.body: Romanian standards: 90×200 (single), 140×200 (compact double), 160×200 (double), 180×200 (king). The mattress is not included — you choose it separately.

info.title: Upholstered bed
info.body: Frame and headboard wrapped in fabric or faux leather. You choose the fabric and colour together with the company.

storage.title: Storage under the bed?
storage.subtitle: A lift-up box or side drawers — the space under the mattress can work.

info.title: Simple bed
info.body: A classic frame with no mechanisms — the simplest and cheapest option.
info.pros1: The lowest price, and nothing that can break
info.pros2: Light — easy to move or take apart
info.cons1: The space under the mattress goes unused

info.title: Gas-lift base
info.body: You lift the mattress on gas pistons and a bed-sized box opens underneath.
info.pros1: The largest hidden storage in the bedroom
info.pros2: Needs no side clearance — works even tight against a wall
info.cons1: The mechanism adds cost, and you lift the mattress every time

info.title: Under-bed drawers
info.body: Two to four drawers along the sides — linens are one pull away.
info.pros1: Easy everyday access — pull the drawer and done
info.pros2: Cheaper than the lift-up mechanism
info.cons1: Drawers need clear floor space beside the bed to open

material.title: What material?
material.subtitle: The frame material (for upholstered beds, the inner structure).

sketch.title: Do you have a room sketch?

configuration.title: How should the dresser be divided?
configuration.subtitle: Drawers only, doors only, or a mix.

info.title: Drawer dresser
info.body: The bedroom classic — everything on its own level. Soft-close drawers earn their keep here.
info.pros1: Each level has its job — nothing gets lost at the back
info.pros2: Pull a drawer out and see everything at a glance
info.cons1: Every drawer means extra slides — the price climbs noticeably

info.title: Mixed dresser
info.body: Drawers for small things, shelved doors for bulky ones — covers both needs.
info.pros1: Small items in drawers, big ones behind doors
info.pros2: More affordable than an all-drawer build
info.cons1: Each zone is smaller — it fills up faster than it looks

info.title: Door dresser
info.body: Doors with shelves behind — the simplest build, so the lowest price.
info.pros1: Hinges only, no slides — the lowest price
info.pros2: Shelves take bulky items, not just folded clothes
info.cons1: Reaching the back means moving what sits in front

tableType.subtitle: Its purpose sets the size and height.

info.title: Rectangular table
info.body: Sits against a wall when you need space, moves to the center for occasions.
info.pros1: Pushed against a wall, it frees the room day to day
info.pros2: The ends seat extra guests easily
info.cons1: Corners get in the way in tight rooms

info.title: Round table
info.body: No corners — safe with small kids, and everyone sees everyone at the table.
info.pros1: No corners for anyone to bump into
info.pros2: Everyone sits at the same distance — conversation flows on its own
info.cons1: For the same seat count it needs more clear space around it

info.title: Extendable table
info.body: Compact day to day, gains 40–80 cm for occasions — a good mechanism makes all the difference.
info.pros1: A table for 4 becomes one for 6–8 in minutes
info.pros2: You don't block the room all year for a few occasions
info.cons1: The mechanism adds cost and a visible seam in the top

info.body: As a guide: 4 people → 120–140 cm, 6 → 160–180 cm, 8+ → over 200 cm. Allow ~60 cm of width per seat.

material.title: What material?
material.subtitle: The tabletop takes the most wear — solid wood lasts and can be refinished.

sketch.title: Do you have a sketch?
sketch.subtitle: Optional — the space where the table will go.

style.title: What type of shoe cabinet?
style.subtitle: The mechanism sets the depth and capacity.

info.body: Tilt-out doors with angled racks — shoes sit almost vertical, so the unit fits any hallway.

info.pros2: Keeps a narrow hallway walkable

info.pros2: Takes tall boots and shoe boxes alike
info.cons1: At ~35 cm deep it noticeably narrows a small hallway

info.body: A low unit with a seat, often upholstered, and storage below — no balancing act.

info.pros2: Seating and storage on the same footprint
info.cons1: The low body holds fewer pairs than a tall cabinet

style.title: What nightstand style?
style.subtitle: With drawers, an open shelf, or wall-mounted.

info.title: Drawer nightstand
info.body: Small things stay hidden, the top stays clear. Soft-close shuts silently at night.
info.pros1: Charger, book, pills — hidden but an arm's reach away
info.pros2: A clear top keeps the bedroom tidy
info.cons1: Slides raise the price over a simple shelf

info.title: Open nightstand
info.body: A simple shelf — reach out and your book or phone is there. Minimal build, minimal price.
info.pros1: The simplest build — the lowest price
info.pros2: Nothing to open — grab and put back in one motion
info.cons1: Whatever you put on it stays in sight

info.title: Floating nightstand
info.body: Fixed to the wall with clear floor below — the room feels airier.
info.pros1: Clear floor — the vacuum passes right under
info.pros2: A light, modern look beside the bed
info.cons1: Needs a solid wall — drywall calls for special anchors

info.title: One or a pair
info.body: A pair balances a double bed; beside a single bed, one is enough.

material.title: What material?
material.subtitle: Usually matched to the bed or the wardrobe.

sketch.title: Do you have a sketch?
sketch.subtitle: Optional — the space next to the bed.

config3d.title: Build your nightstand in 3D
config3d.subtitle: Adjust the dimensions and pick the mix of drawers and open zones.

style.title: What type of bench?
style.subtitle: With a storage box, with shoe space, or simple.

info.title: Storage bench
info.body: Lift the seat and there is a full box below — blankets, seasonal shoes, toys.
info.pros1: A whole box of storage, invisible from the room
info.pros2: Seating and storage on the same footprint
info.cons1: The lift mechanism makes it the priciest bench type

info.title: Bench with shoe rack
info.body: An open rack under the seat — everyday shoes at hand, no doors to open.
info.pros1: Slip your shoes off and shelve them in one motion
info.pros2: Simple build, price to match
info.cons1: Shoes stay in sight — the hallway needs a little discipline

info.title: Simple bench
info.body: Just the seat, nothing more — at the foot of the bed or in the hallway.
info.pros1: The most affordable option
info.pros2: Light — move it wherever a seat is needed
info.cons1: No storage at all

info.title: Upholstered seat
info.body: A fixed cushion wrapped in fabric — comfortable while you put shoes on. You pick the fabric with the company.

sketch.subtitle: Optional — the space where the bench will go.

data.h: 2. What data we collect and why
data.b:
We collect and store the following categories of data:

• Account data: name, email address, password (stored encrypted), language preference — to create and manage your account.
• Request data: project description, delivery/installation address, city and county, chosen contact channels (email, phone) — to publish the request and, once claimed, to share with the Companies working on it.
• Company data: company name, tax ID, addresses, team — to verify and display the company in the Platform.
• The content of conversations held in the Platform (stored encrypted) and uploaded files — to run messaging and offers.
• Technical and usage data: IP address, device type, pages visited and actions performed in the Platform.

The legal bases are contract performance (providing the service), legitimate interest (security and improving the Platform) and, where required by law, your consent.

usage.b: We analyse how the Platform is used (pages visited, features used, errors encountered) to understand what works and what needs improvement. These analyses use aggregated or pseudonymised data wherever possible and are not aimed at building individual profiles for purposes other than product improvement and service security.

marketing.b:
With your consent, we may send you commercial communications about the Platform (news, features, offers) and may use usage data for more relevant marketing and advertising campaigns.

You can withdraw your consent at any time, with immediate effect: from your account settings, via the unsubscribe link present in every email, or by writing to [EMAIL CONTACT]. Withdrawing consent does not affect your normal use of the Platform.

sharing.b:
Request data (including your name and contact channels) is shared exclusively with the Companies that claimed your request, so they can contact you and send offers.

We use infrastructure providers (hosting, file storage, email delivery) that process data on our behalf under GDPR-compliant contracts. We do not sell your personal data to third parties.

rights.b:
You have the right of access to your data, the right to rectification, the right to erasure (“right to be forgotten”), the right to restrict processing, the right to data portability, the right to object (including to marketing) and the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing.

To exercise these rights, write to [EMAIL CONTACT]; we reply within one month at the latest. If you consider that the processing breaches the law, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the Romanian supervisory authority (ANSPDCP, www.dataprotection.ro).

retention.b:
We keep account data for as long as the account is active. When the account is deleted, personal data is deleted or anonymised within a reasonable period, except for data we are legally required to keep (for example accounting records) and data strictly necessary to defend legal claims.

Technical usage data is kept for limited periods, proportionate to the purpose it was collected for.

cookies.b:
The Platform uses strictly necessary cookies: session authentication (httpOnly cookies) and remembering your chosen language (RO/EN).

We currently use no third-party advertising cookies. If we introduce non-essential cookies (for example for analytics or marketing), we will ask for your consent beforehand and update this section.
